messages:
sam: Heads-up — multiple customers hit 429s this morning while the metering dashboard shows they were well under quota. Happened around 10:06-10:08 UTC. Suspect ingestion lag + enforcement race.

sam: sample logs:
```
[2026-11-01T10:07:12Z] enforcer: key=org_42 token_bucket=0.0 allowed=false
[2026-11-01T10:07:12Z] api-gateway: accepted request id=abcd123 org=org_42 tokens=120
[2026-11-01T10:07:12Z] metering-ingest: queued event org_42 tokens=120 offset=3421
[2026-11-01T10:07:14Z] metering-processor: wrote batch for org_42 ts=2026-11-01T10:06:50 latency=1100ms
```

anjali: Thanks — I saw the spike on the metrics. Consumer group cg-meter-processor was behind (~90-120s) due to GC pauses on the consumer host. When processor writes the batch late, reconciliation runs every 5m so enforcement doesn't see the credit fast enough.

kevin: Right — enforcement uses a fast path: in-memory token bucket + Redis counter updated by the stream consumer. If the consumer lags, Redis is stale and enforcer blocks. Two failure modes: (1) late metering events -> customers get blocked, (2) duplicate/delayed replays -> potential double-charging unless we dedupe.

marta: Kafka partition 3 had a leadership bounce around 10:05 which spiked consumer lag. Ops already restarted the host but there was a ~2m window.

kevin: Short-term mitigations: 
- enable "mismatch_shadow_mode" for affected tiers (log mismatches without blocking)
- bump per-org burst_override by +200 tokens for paid tiers for 1 hour
- alert if enforcer 429 rate > threshold AND metering lag > 30s

sam: Can we do that via the internal config API?

kevin: Yes. Example quick change (run from ops machine):
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://console.internal.redwood/api/enforcer/config \
  -d '{"selector":{"tier":"paid"},"overrides":{"burst_override":200,"mismatch_mode":"shadow"}}'
```

devon: For a safer long-term fix I propose a hybrid write-ahead: when the gateway accepts a request, it emits a small write-ahead delta to Redis (or a durable fast store) that the enforcer checks for immediate accounting, while the full event still goes to the metering stream for billing. That gives enforcement a low-latency source and the stream remains the source-of-record.

anjali: Agree with write-ahead but watch consistency. Need idempotency keys on the write-ahead (request_id) and a TTL (~30s) so we don't persist forever. Also the write-ahead should be opt-in per route (configurable) to limit QPS impact.

kevin: Other design details:
- event ids + dedupe window (24h) in the processor to avoid double-apply on replay/backfill
- compensating credits: when processor finally ingests late events, it should emit negative deltas to reconcile enforcer counters if necessary (or mark events as "late_applied" and the enforcer subtracts).
- improve consumer visibility: expose consumer lag per-partition in console with per-org tail link.

marta: I'll run a replay of the affected partition to reprocess offsets 3418-3435 and verify the backfill. Plan: run in dry-run mode first and emit diffs to /tmp/metering-replay-diffs.json.

devon: For billing, prefer compensating credits to avoid charging twice. Implementation: processor writes a compensating event type = "credit_adjustment" with reason = "late_ingest_reconciliation" and reference_event_id.

sam: ACTIONS:
- kevin: prototype write-ahead flow and a small proof-of-concept in staging (ETA: 48h)
- marta: run partition replay dry-run now, then actual backfill if diffs look good (ETA: 2h)
- devon: start spec for compensating credits and idempotency (ETA: EOD)
- sam: monitor 429 rate, enable shadow override for paid tiers now and roll back after verification

ops-bot: Incident INC-20261101-07 created, priority=P2 — assignees=kevin,marta,sam

kevin: Also adding a small metric: enforcer_mismatch_ratio = enforcer_blocks / (enforcer_blocks + metering_reconciled_blocks). Will add dashboard tile and an alert for >2% sustained.

anjali: Good. One more thing — add consumer health checks to the rollout UX so canary steps block if consumer lag > 5s for the first minute. Prevents new deploys from masking regressions.

sam: Thanks all. Will post an update once marta finishes the replay.
